subject.title: fix: sleep tool — session-targeted wake, correct sandbox policy, doc fixes

question: Should OpenClaw permanently add a separate built-in `sleep` tool, or keep delayed same-session follow-ups on the existing cron surface?
rationale: The PR adds a permanent model-facing core API parallel to an existing supported scheduling capability, and code review cannot decide whether the ergonomic benefit justifies another privileged tool contract. citeturn11view3

options.title: Keep cron canonical
options.body: Do not add the parallel core tool; improve cron prompting or documentation if delayed follow-ups need better discoverability.

options.title: Sponsor the sleep API
options.body: Accept the new tool direction only after it inherits owner authorization, supports embedded runs, implements interruption and restart semantics, and receives live proof.

recommendation.title: Keep cron canonical
recommendation.body: Do not add the parallel core tool; improve cron prompting or documentation if delayed follow-ups need better discoverability.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history most strongly connects this person to the agent-runtime and cron policy surfaces that define the permanent API boundary. citeturn16search2turn5view5
